scope: Isolated frontend with synthetic command replies and a stubbed emergency audio handler; no real emergency playback.
checks: Start uses a named modal warning without sending a command or starting audio
Starting has a red header, darker two-pixel border and warning symbol
The explanation names every host, exactly one page per host, immediate playback and the 20-second repeat
The tournament page subscribes to host-specific emergency playback
Both actions sit in the footer and cancellation is focused by default
Repeated trigger activation cannot create another confirmation
Cancelling changes neither emergency state nor the free-text draft and restores focus
Escape dismisses the warning without output
Enter on the initially focused action cancels rather than starts the emergency
Explicit start sends exactly the tournament and intended action and shows a busy trigger
A pending start cannot be submitted twice
Request failure keeps the inactive state, preserves the draft and permits retry
Successful start displays the stop action only after the simulated live notification
Stopping is a yellow warning with a dark border and the matching action labels
The stop dialog explains current playback and automatic repetition
Cancelling stop keeps playback enabled without sending a stop
Explicit stop sends enable false once and shows progress
Successful stop restores the initial action without sending free text
A tournament-wide start notification cannot bypass the host-specific playback grant
A start notification from another device dismisses an obsolete start warning
A stop notification also dismisses an obsolete stop warning
The approval guard cannot invert an emergency state that changed during confirmation
Approval after a tournament change sends nothing to either tournament
Emergency start fits the viewport at 1920x1080
Emergency start keeps its heading and actions visible at 1920x1080
